It is obvious to us that the US Federal Government is now gripping down tighter on the economy than it ever has in order to make it appear afloat. I am relatively young and all my life it has appeared like "the greatest country in the world" was just buying time, economically speaking. The recent technological revolution (~ past 20 years) centered in the US obviously fueled the US economy in a major way.

Is it possible that if Silicon Valley had sprung up in Tokyo or London, that the US economy would have already crumbled?

(I understand that many cities are technology hubs. Also, I realize this is difficult to try to estimate but I just wanted to get some good discussion going.)
Technology Economy and a Failing US Federal Government

I think that the economy is sufficiently diversified that the US economy would not have crumbled. The US still maintains a strong grip on financial markets, for example. I also believe that the "technological revolution" you speak of is global, albeit centered in the US, but this improvement of technology has strongly affected capital markets and improved economies across the world. It's especially affected those labour markets involved in the production of technological materials (e.g. East and South Asia). I think the US entrepreneurship model and amounts of skilled labour would still have led the US to be involved in this technological revolution.

this improvement of technology has strongly affected capital markets and improved economies across the world. It's especially affected those labour markets involved in the production of technological materials

This is a great point. It is a technological progress feedback loop of sorts.

To take this into a different direction, many people I have come across describe the invention of computers and computer networking as having come directly from the offices at D/ARPA. If it hadn't been for the US Federal budget and willingness to invest large sums into these experiments, how much of a delay (if any) would we have seen before the market created computers?
